acceptance: A test asserts the DuckDB spec's --dry-run output equals a golden copy captured from the pre-change script: all 123 emitted commands in order, with separate assertions of 116 benchmark invocations and 7 driver installs

Re-analyzing the archived DuckDB manifest gives byte-identical analysis JSON and CSV and identical median-bundle content to the archived outputs (or every difference is listed and explained in the PR)
Existing tests in tests/unit/scripts/test_duckdb_version_matrix.py pass unchanged, or each changed assertion is justified in the PR body
Docs that name the old scripts are updated or still accurate
description:
scripts/run_duckdb_version_matrix.py and scripts/analyze_duckdb_version_matrix.py hard-code DuckDB versions, benchmarks, database clearing and the pre-release rule. A second engine needs the same machinery, so extend rather than copy: move the engine-specific parts into a per-engine spec (platform, versions, benchmarks with scale factors, per-cell setup and cleanup, pre-release handling, required validation status), and keep DuckDB as one spec.

Guardrails:
- DuckDB reproducibility is the blocking test: for the DuckDB spec, the new runner's --dry-run must emit exactly the same 116 commands, in the same order, as today's script at HEAD d076a974d.
- The analyzer must give identical analysis JSON and CSV, and identical median bundles, when run on the archived DuckDB manifest at ~/Developer/benchmark_runs/duckdb-version-matrix-20260829-sf10-v2/matrix-manifest.json.
- Keep the old script paths working (as thin wrappers or documented replacements), and update every reference to them: results-data/SEED_CORPUS_SPEC.md, results-data/CORPUS_NOTES.md, and tests/unit/scripts/test_duckdb_version_matrix.py.
- No Polars-specific behaviour in this item; that belongs to pvm-s3b.
